question.text: Considering the following reaction sequence, the correct statement(s) is(are)

options.text: Compounds <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi></math> are carboxylic acids.

Compounds <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi></math> react with hydroxylamine to give the corresponding oximes.
Compound <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></math> reacts with dialkylcadmium to give the corresponding tertiary alcohol.

solution.text:
Benzene undergoes friedel craft's reaction with succinic anhydride in presence of anhydrous AlCl3 to form P.The mechanism of the reaction is electrophilic substitution.

The keto group in P gets reduced on reaction Zn/Hg in HCl to form Q that is 4-phenylbutanoic acid.

This reacts with thionyl chloride to form R, that is 

4-Phenylbutanoyl chloride.

R again undergoes friedel craft's reaction to form S.

S gets reduced on reaction Zn/Hg in HCl to form a hydrocarbon as given in the reactions below.

Compound S can not decolorizes bromine water.

R2Cd is a less reactive nucleophile so reaction stops at carbonyl group.

Due to the presence of carbonyl group both P and S forms oxime with hydroxyl amine.
